chapters.title: Adi Parva — The Book of the Beginning

verses.sanskrit:
नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम् ।
देवीं सरस्वतीं चैव ततो जयमुदीरयेत् ॥
verses.translation: Having bowed to Narayana and Nara, the best of men, and also to the goddess Sarasvati, one should then recite the Jaya (Mahabharata).

verses.sanskrit:
यद्भागवतं ज्ञानं विज्ञानसमन्वितम् ।
व्यासदेवकृतं भारतं सर्वशास्त्रेषु पूज्यते ॥
verses.translation: The Bharata, composed by Vyasadeva, endowed with divine knowledge and wisdom, is revered among all scriptures.

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मे चार्थे च कामे च मोक्षे च भरतर्षभ ।
यदिहास्ति तदन्यत्र यन्नेहास्ति न तत्क्वचित् ॥
verses.translation: In matters of dharma, artha (wealth), kama (desire), and moksha (liberation) — whatever is found here may be found elsewhere, but what is not found here is found nowhere.

chapters.title: Sabha Parva — The Book of the Assembly Hall

verses.sanskrit:
ततो द्यूतमयं क्रीडां शकुनिर्मायया करोत् ।
पाण्डवानां श्रियं राज्यं यां चापि द्रौपदीमपि ॥
verses.translation: Then Shakuni, through deception, arranged the game of dice, by which the Pandavas lost their wealth, kingdom, and even Draupadi.

verses.sanskrit:
सभामध्ये द्रौपद्याः वस्त्रापहरणं कृतम् ।
कृष्णाय शरणं गत्वा रक्षितासौ महात्मना ॥
verses.translation: In the midst of the assembly, the disrobing of Draupadi was attempted. Taking refuge in Krishna, she was protected by the great soul.

chapters.title: Vana Parva — The Book of the Forest

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वनवासं प्राप्ताः पाण्डवाः सत्यविक्रमाः ।
द्वादश वर्षाणि वने वासं चक्रुर्महावनेषु ॥
verses.translation: Then the Pandavas, of true valor, having been sent to exile, spent twelve years dwelling in the great forests.

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिरो धर्मराजो नलोपाख्यानमश्रृणोत् ।
धर्मं च ज्ञानमैश्वर्यं सत्यं चैव यथारथम् ॥
verses.translation: Yudhishthira, the righteous king, heard the Nala episode and learned about dharma, knowledge, divine power, and truth in their true form.

chapters.title: Virata Parva — The Book of Virata

verses.sanskrit:
ततो विराटनगरे अज्ञातवासं चक्रिरे ।
पाण्डवाः सर्वे राजन् छद्मनाऽवनिपालयन् ॥
verses.translation: Then in the city of Virata, all the Pandavas lived incognito, O King, guarding their identities in disguise.

chapters.title: Udyoga Parva — The Book of Effort

verses.sanskrit:
तत्र कृष्णो महाबाहुर्दूतो धर्मसुतस्य ह ।
गत्वा कौरवसभायां शान्तिं प्रायाचत ॥
verses.translation: There, the mighty-armed Krishna, as the envoy of the son of Dharma (Yudhishthira), went to the Kaurava assembly and sought peace.

verses.sanskrit:
विदुरो वाक्यमब्रवीत् धृतराष्ट्रं महीपतिम् ।
पाण्डवैः सह सन्धिं कुरु राजन् युद्धं मा कराः ॥
verses.translation: Vidura spoke these words to King Dhritarashtra: 'O King, make peace with the Pandavas. Do not wage war.'

chapters.title: Bhishma Parva — The Book of Bhishma

verses.sanskrit:
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः ।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥
verses.translation: Dhritarashtra said: O Sanjaya, after my sons and the sons of Pandu assembled in the holy field of Kurukshetra, desiring to fight, what did they do?

verses.sanskrit:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verses.translation: You have a right to perform your prescribed duty, but you are not entitled to the fruits of action. Never consider yourself the cause of the results, and never be attached to inaction.

verses.sanskrit:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत ।
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥
verses.translation: Whenever and wherever there is a decline in dharma, O descendant of Bharata, and a predominant rise of adharma — at that time I manifest Myself.

verses.sanskrit:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् ।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ॥
verses.translation: To deliver the pious and to annihilate the miscreants, as well as to reestablish the principles of dharma, I advent Myself millennium after millennium.

chapters.title: Drona Parva — The Book of Drona

verses.sanskrit:
अश्वत्थामा हतः इति कुञ्जरः ।
युधिष्ठिरो धर्मराजो वम्शः तस्य न मृषा ॥
verses.translation: Ashwatthama is dead — the elephant. Yudhishthira, the king of dharma, uttered these words, and his chariot that always floated above the ground descended.

chapters.title: Karna Parva — The Book of Karna

verses.sanskrit:
कर्णो महारथो वीरः सूतपुत्रो महाबलः ।
दानवीरः सदा दाता कवचकुण्डलधारकः ॥
verses.translation: Karna, the great warrior, heroic and mighty, son of the charioteer, ever generous, who gave away even his natural armor and earrings.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुनेन हतः कर्णः कुरुक्षेत्रे महाहवे ।
मित्रद्रोही न कर्णोऽभूत् दैवे कर्मविपर्ययः ॥
verses.translation: Karna was slain by Arjuna in the great battle of Kurukshetra. Karna was no traitor to friendship — it was the reversal of fate and karma.

chapters.title: Shalya Parva — The Book of Shalya

verses.sanskrit:
शल्यं हत्वा महाराजं भीमसेनो महाबलः ।
दुर्योधनं गदायुद्धे जघान कुरुनन्दनम् ॥
verses.translation: The mighty Bhimasena slew King Shalya, and in a mace duel, destroyed Duryodhana, the joy of the Kuru dynasty.

chapters.title: Shanti Parva — The Book of Peace

verses.sanskrit:
शरशय्यागतो भीष्मो युधिष्ठिरमुवाच ह ।
धर्मं चार्थं च कामं च मोक्षं चैव चतुर्विधम् ॥
verses.translation: Bhishma, lying on his bed of arrows, spoke to Yudhishthira about the four goals of life: dharma, artha, kama, and moksha.

verses.sanskrit:
अहिंसा परमो धर्मस्तथाहिंसा परं तपः ।
अहिंसा परमं दानम् अहिंसा परमं फलम् ॥
verses.translation: Non-violence is the highest dharma. Non-violence is the highest penance. Non-violence is the greatest charity. Non-violence is the supreme fruit.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः ।
येनाक्रमन्त्यृषयो ह्याप्तकामा यत्र तत्सत्यस्य परमं निधानम् ॥
verses.translation: Truth alone triumphs, not falsehood. Through truth, the divine path is laid out, by which the sages, whose desires have been fulfilled, reach the supreme abode of Truth.
